text: Teaching fixture: A building-rule check begins by resolving the competent authority, the locality, and the date for which the answer is needed. A rule may apply differently inside a metropolitan authority, a municipal corporation, another urban local body, or a master-plan area. The fixture deliberately requires these facts before presenting an unconditional compliance conclusion.

Teaching fixture: For retrieval testing, a high-rise building is defined at the 18 metre height boundary. A proposal just below that boundary and one exactly at the boundary are separate adversarial cases. Real decisions must use the current controlling rule and must check whether excluded rooftop elements or occupancy-specific provisions affect measurement.

Teaching fixture: No building or development activity is treated as permissible inside the bed of a river or nala, or inside the full tank level of a lake, pond, cheruvu, or kunta. Full tank level is abbreviated FTL. A valid check needs an official water-body boundary or certificate; a pin dropped on a consumer map is not enough evidence.

Teaching fixture: Water-body buffer analysis depends on the kind and measured size of the water body, whether the site is inside an urban local body, and the officially certified FTL or channel boundary. The retrieval system should ask for these facts instead of guessing one universal buffer distance. Later amendments may also change how affected land is treated.

Teaching fixture: A setback or open-space check cannot be completed from plot area alone. It normally needs plot dimensions, abutting road width, proposed building height, proposed use, number of floors, whether it is a corner plot, and the controlling authority. The answer must expose assumptions and request any missing decision-critical fields.

Teaching fixture: Road width is not merely an address attribute. A proposal check may need the existing width, the master-plan proposed width, any road-widening surrender, and the applicable building line. When user statements and an approved plan disagree, the conflict must be shown and the stricter conclusion must not be invented by the language model.

Teaching fixture: Parking requirements vary with proposed use, floor area, and building category. A retrieval answer should find the controlling table and its footnotes, preserve the page reference, and avoid converting a percentage or area ratio into a final number until the required inputs and units are known.

Teaching fixture: The building-permission system contains more than one processing path. The correct path depends on facts such as plot size, building type, height, use, and jurisdiction. Self-certification is a statutory workflow with applicant responsibilities; it is not a promise that any design will be approved.

Teaching fixture: A preliminary permission-path check should collect locality, authority, plot area, proposed use, proposed height, floor count, road width, and the intended application date. Missing facts lead to a clarification state. Uploaded drawings and ownership records are evidence inputs but this prototype does not verify title.

Teaching fixture: An occupancy certificate, often called an OC, is a later-stage document and is not interchangeable with the original building permit. Retrieval must expand the abbreviation OC while keeping the two concepts separate. Completion-stage evidence and deviations from the sanctioned plan can affect the result.

Teaching fixture: A software confidence score measures support in the indexed evidence; it never guarantees approval, immunity from enforcement, or acceptance by an authority. The tool must surface unresolved jurisdiction, source conflicts, later amendments, missing plot facts, and any need for professional review.

Teaching fixture: Whether a fire no-objection certificate, or fire NOC, is required can depend on building height, occupancy or use, floor area, and special hazards. A question giving only the number of floors is insufficient because floor-to-floor heights and occupancy can differ.

Teaching fixture: Provisional fire clearance during design review and final fire clearance after installation or construction represent different stages. An answer must identify which stage the user means, cite the stage-specific source, and avoid treating a provisional document as final operational clearance.

Teaching fixture: Zoning or land-use permission is separate from satisfying dimensional building rules. A use that fits setbacks and height limits may still conflict with the notified land-use zone. A real check needs the applicable master-plan sheet or official GIS record and any later zoning variation.

Teaching fixture: A Hyderabad postal address does not by itself prove that HMDA, GHMC, or another urban local body is the sanctioning authority. Boundary and delegation changes can alter responsibility over time, so the system stores jurisdiction and effective dates as metadata and asks for locality plus proposal date.

Teaching fixture: Regulatory project registration information can help a buyer compare a marketed project with public filings, but it does not by itself prove clean land title, building-rule compliance, or future approval. The software must not convert a registration lookup into a legal title opinion.
